title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code / Cowork ship fleet-hygiene fixes that hit our exact failure modes — /doctor now diagnoses and repairs, scheduled tasks no longer duplicate-fire on wake, Cowork VM-mode login fixed
bullets.summary: /doctor moved from a read-only report to interactive repair: checks installation health, finds unused skills / MCP servers / plugins weighed against their context cost, deduplicates local CLAUDE.md against checked-in ones, proposes trimming derivable CLAUDE.md content, and flags slow hooks — asking before it changes anything. Alongside: a fix for scheduled tasks firing many duplicate runs at once when the computer wakes from sleep, and a fix for Cowork VM-mode local-agent sessions failing with 'Not logged in / Please run /login' on CLI 2.1.203+.
bullets.how: Maintenance for The Construct's own fleet, not theory. We run a large installed-skills registry and a wide MCP surface, and the context-cost audit is exactly the pruning signal the daily/weekly new-skills scan lacks. The duplicate-fire-on-wake fix matters directly — this brief, the Lens Harvard scan, and the PRAGMA visibility scan are all sleep-straddling scheduled tasks that stood to double-run. Run /doctor against the Construct config this week and let it flag the dead weight.

bullets.title: The MCP spec goes stateless on July 28 — the handshake and session ID are removed, and every server we run has 13 days to be ready
bullets.summary: The release candidate is locked and the final spec publishes Jul 28. The initialize/initialized handshake is gone; protocol version, client info and client capabilities now travel in _meta on every request, with a new server/discover method for clients that want capabilities up front. The Mcp-Session-Id header and the protocol-level session are removed, so any request can land on any server instance — no sticky routing, no shared session store, plain round-robin works. Six SEPs deliver the change; extensions (MCP Apps, Tasks) become first-class, plus auth hardening and a real deprecation policy. Tier 1 SDKs are expected to ship support inside the ten-week validation window.
bullets.how: This is the floor moving under bullets 1 and 3. Not breaking news (the RC locked in May), but it earns the slot today because it is 13 days out and nobody has checked our surface against it. Every MCP server The Construct depends on — and every one we'd put in front of a PRAGMA client — either follows its SDK through the window or breaks. Pairs with /doctor: prune the fleet first, then pin which survivors are on Tier 1 SDKs and which are hand-rolled and now our problem. The stateless move is also quietly good news — it makes a client-hosted managed MCP dramatically cheaper to run.

bullets.title: Rafay ships a managed MCP server that enforces existing RBAC and project boundaries — governed MCP arrives as a product category
bullets.summary: Announced yesterday: Rafay connects AI assistants to its governed operational context through a standard protocol while enforcing the same RBAC and project boundaries teams already use, rather than handing agents an unscoped connection.
bullets.how: This is the shape our own MCP fleet should take. We currently authorize connectors per-surface with no unified boundary model — fine at our size, indefensible at a client's. 'Managed MCP with the client's existing permission model enforced at the server' is a concrete PRAGMA deliverable, and it pairs with /doctor's audit: prune the surface, then bound what's left.

bullets.title: Anthropic ships Claude for Teachers — the sellable unit is a skills pack + curriculum connections + a data-governance addendum, given away free
bullets.summary: Verified US K-12 educators get free premium Claude access bundled with teaching skills and curriculum connections aligned to standards in all 50 states; Teachers data is excluded from model training and student data is governed by a FERPA-compliant K-12 Data Processing Addendum, with a pilot evaluation in Detroit Public Schools Community District.
bullets.how: Read it as packaging, not education. The vertical bundle is skills + domain data connections + an explicit data-governance instrument — and the governance instrument is what makes it adoptable inside a regulated institution. That's the template for a PRAGMA vertical pack (signage, real estate, contractors): a named skill set, wired-in domain sources, and a written data posture. The addendum is a feature, not paperwork.

bullets.title: GPT-5.6 becomes the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot and auto-enables for all eligible commercial users on July 24 unless an admin blocks it
bullets.summary: The Sol/Terra/Luna family is now default across Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Chat; rollout is opt-out rather than opt-in, with mandatory enablement Jul 24.
bullets.how: The point isn't the model, it's the default. Every SMB client of ours on M365 gets a materially different AI in their Office apps on Jul 24 without asking for it, and most won't notice until output changes. That's a free PRAGMA conversation opener — 'do you know what changed in your Copilot last week, and who decided?' — and a reminder that our own routing stays provider-agnostic precisely so nobody flips our defaults for us.

praxis_lesson: Today's items are one sequence, and the calendar just put dates on it: audit, bound, package. /doctor's context-cost audit says prune the fleet; the Jul 28 stateless spec says the protocol under that fleet changes in 13 days whether or not we look; Rafay says bound what survives with the permission model the client already trusts; Claude for Teachers says the sellable unit is never the model — it's a bounded skill pack plus a written governance posture. The quiet frontier is the tell: when no new flagship lands, the work that pays is infrastructure you already own and forgot to inspect. Two hard dates now sit inside two weeks — Jul 24 flips our clients' Copilot, Jul 28 moves our own floor. PRAGMA sells the instrument, not the intelligence, and an instrument nobody has calibrated is a liability.
